newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares fell in profit-taking for the third session running after reaching successive 33-month highs and analysts said the main market, currently at 16,167.9 points, would fall again on Friday.
"The fall could continue to about 16,000 points ... with tomorrow's fall smaller than today's," said Maciej Matusiak, of PKO BP brokerage, referring to Thursday's 0.8-percent dip.
Some analysts said the market could bottom out closer to 15,000 points before rebounding, signalled by the market's failure to rise on Thursday despite Wednesday's stronger buying after price-fixing.

"It looked like the correction would be short, but it (Wednesday's dominant buying after price-fixing) represented speculators expecting to gain on one session of growth within the correction," said Pawel Hominski of Magnus brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.8 percent to 16,167.9 points and turnover fell 25.4 percent to 158.9 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said Thursday's statistical office (GUS) estimate of a six-percent growth last year might not affect the market as such a figure had been expected.
Analysts attributed top gainer Stalexport's 6.1 percent surge to its winning of a concession on Wednesday to modernise and operate a 60km section of toll highway.
They said Prochnik fell 6.1 percent in profit taking after surging when a court cleared the sale of 10 percent of its stock to a National Investment Fund (NFI).
NFI units fell 1.3 percent to 148 zlotys in 29.6- million-zloty regular bourse trade and fell two percent to 144.5 zlotys in 25.9-million-zloty continuous trade.
Continuous trade was at 14 million zlotys with three stocks up, three down and seven flat.-- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
